children: U.S. airline Delta Air Lines Inc. (DAL, Financials) slumped over 4% increased fuel prices that obscured solid travel demand and prompted the company to reduce its full-year profit projection.
Adjusted sales rose 16 percent to $17.6 billion in the third quarter from $15.2 billion a year earlier, missing Wall Street expectations of $17.65 billion.
Adjusted profits increased to $1.72 a share from $1.71 but fell short of the $1.82 average expectation. The real trouble was gasoline.

Delta's adjusted fuel expenditure rose 62% to $4.1 billion, including nearly $500 million more than management had forecast in early July. Now the corporation anticipates its 2026 gasoline expense to rise by almost $6 billion.
That pressure has led Delta to decrease its full-year EPS target to $5.10-$5.60 from $6.50-$7.50. Expected free cash flow also dropped to $2.5 billion from the prior $3 billion-$4 billion range.
Demand is good. Passenger revenue was up 18%, cargo revenue was up 29% and maintenance, repair and overhaul income was up 28%.
their leaves investors with a tricky divide: Customers are still going but more of their money is being eaten up by gasoline.
Delta estimates earnings per share of $1.15 to $1.65 for the December quarter, depending on gasoline at about $4.25 a gallon. Energy costs are the biggest variable to watch.

title: Delta's Fuel Bill Just Changed the Story
